summary.headline: Indiabulls FY26 PAT of INR346 crores; Q4 FY26 PAT INR195 crores (INR194.26 crores per correction) led by first real estate revenue recognition.
summary.overview: Indiabulls Ltd (formerly Yaari Digital) resumed earnings calls after a long gap, reporting FY26 revenue of about INR879 crores and PAT of INR346 crores, with Q4 FY26 revenue of INR417 crores and PAT of INR195 crores. Management said Q4 was the first quarter of real estate revenue recognition in the books and that the group has exited digital lending and e-commerce after merging 17 group entities. The company now runs two verticals, real estate and financial services, with real estate expected to deliver about 80% of group profit. Management guided real estate profits to at least double in FY27 and triple in FY28, though it declined quarterly guidance. The transcript carries annotations that correct several figures (FY26 revenue INR880.78 crores, Q4 revenue INR418.39 crores, Q4 PAT INR194.26 crores).

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Expected to contribute nearly 80% of group profit; total GDV potential about INR21,000 crores plus and sellable area over 1.1 crore sq ft across Gurugram, Mumbai and Ludhiana. FY26 sales about 21.6 lakh sq ft; revenue recognised on percentage-completion basis, starting Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Financial Services - Broking
segments.commentary: Profitable, with about INR28 crores PBT in FY26 from the offline branch business. Online discount broking being built with a new team; 28,000 customers added in Q4 FY26; Algo platform launched.

segments.name: Financial Services - Asset Reconstruction (ARC)
segments.commentary: Fee-paying AUM INR622 crores and assets under allocation INR3,794 crores; about 2,200 collection staff on payroll. Management said the first year is absorbed by collections against acquisition cost, with profits from FY27.

segments.name: SMB investment (SpringCash, US)
segments.commentary: Treated as an investment, not a P&L business; stake acquired about 6 months earlier at a $30 million valuation, with about $100 million of disbursals reported by the company.

segments.name: NBFC (legacy Dhani book)
segments.commentary: Loan book about INR1,000 crores with zero debt; no fresh disbursements planned in FY26 or FY27; book is in run-off and expected to be collected as loans mature.

guidance_outlook: Real estate profits expected to grow at least 2x in FY27 versus FY26, and at least 3x in FY28 versus FY27 (as stated).
Management said it is difficult to give quarter-to-quarter guidance.
Around 40 lakh sq ft of launches planned in FY27 with GDV of INR6,000 plus crores; future pipeline of 42 lakh sq ft valued at INR11,900 plus crores.
Over the next 5 to 7 years, management said it could easily cross INR1,000-1,500 crores of PAT (CEO's view).

Indiabulls Tower Prabhadevi (Worli) expected to take 3-4 years to complete; capex about INR600 crores; annual rent about INR1,000 crores as stated, corrected to INR100-120 crores based on market rates.
GDV conversion into P&L expected over about seven years, with construction money flowing into the balance sheet by FY30-32.
capex_capacity: Indiabulls Tower, Prabhadevi (Mumbai): leased commercial asset, about 2.5 lakh sellable sq ft, construction started, capex about INR600 crores, rental income from year 4.
Upcoming launches of about 40 lakh sq ft in FY27 (GDV INR6,000 plus crores), plus future pipeline of 42 lakh sq ft (INR11,900 plus crores).
Key FY26 launches: Indiabulls Estate and Club Sector 104 (over 75% of phase 1 sold), Indiabulls Heights Sector 104 (nearly 100% sold within a week), Indiabulls Green Avenue (plotted, NCR).
Management said 20% of GDV is typically attributable to JV partners.
demand_pricing: Management said launched projects have appreciated about 15% from launch price and it sees no price downward revision.
About 80% recovery on all sold real estate units; buyers who miss payment windows have units cancelled.
Management said the online broking market is large and an entrant with good product and tech stack can grow; broking had 'suffered' during three years of restructuring.

qa_highlights.question: What litigations and contingent liabilities exist across the 17 subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 17 subsidiaries were shut down during the merger, have no litigations or financial liabilities, and that all legacy cases are resolved.

qa_highlights.question: How is revenue recognised for real estate, and what drives PAT growth from INR600-700 crores to INR1,200 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on percentage completion. Growth is driven by real estate, with about 40 lakh sq ft launching in FY27 and a further 1.1 crore sq ft in hand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NBFC book's debt, cash position and NPA known?
qa_highlights.answer: NBFC and group have zero debt; cash and equivalents about INR750 crores; gross NPA about 1%, with legacy losses written off and assets sold to ARCs.

qa_highlights.question: Are PAT guidance figures PBT or PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PBT and PAT will be the same because of a tax shield of about INR3,000 crores in revenue inherited in the merger, until PBT reaches that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and timeline for the Worli/Prabhadevi commercial asset?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction has started; completion expected in 3-4 years; capex about INR600 crores; rental from year 4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GDV inclusive of JV partner share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, GDV includes JV partners; their share is roughly 20%, per management. Conversion to balance sheet expected by about FY30-32.

qa_highlights.question: Why has broking not grown relative to new entrants, and what is the SpringCash valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slow growth to three years of restructuring and said a new online discount broking team is being built. SpringCash was invested at a $30 million valuation about six months ago, and management expects further fundraises at higher valuations.

risks_watch: Real estate earnings depend on project launches, approvals and POC revenue recognition; receivables may build ahead of cash collection, per the analyst's question.
Management reiterated no quarterly guidance; FY27 2x and FY28 3x targets are untested.
Legacy NBFC book (about INR1,000 crores) has no fresh disbursement; recoverability and gross NPA of about 1% are management estimates.
Broking growth lagged peers; new online platform and products are still being launched, with the UPI and PPI licences expected in the current quarter.
Q4 PAT of INR195 crores in the transcript differs from the corrected INR194.26 crores; the INR143 crores profit figure is not reconciled in the call.
Tax shield: PBT equals PAT only until about INR3,000 crores of PBT, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on real estate growth and multi-year targets, but evasive on quantified detail: quarterly guidance was declined, broking growth was framed as future, and several figures were stated loosely and later corrected in annotations.
key_quotes: Real estate is the dominant earning driver and is expected to contribute nearly 80% of group profit.
Q4 FY26 marks the first quarter of real estate revenue recognition in the company's books.
Recognizing that profitability and preservation of capital is non -negotiable at Indiabulls, we exited these businesses.
So definitely we don't see any price downward revision happening.
